You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the rhombohedral space group R-3m, number 166, with Hall symbol -R 3 2". The supplied input cell is a primitive rhombohedral setting with all three lattice vectors equal in length, a = b = c = 5.05234447 Å for the first two axes and 5.05234518 Å for the third, and with all three interaxial angles essentially equal: α = β = 33.1593968° for the first two angles and γ = 33.15938813°. This small departure from exact equality reflects the input cell as given rather than an idealized conventional cell. The declared input composition contains one lithium atom, one iron atom, and two oxygen atoms, for four atoms total in the primitive input cell.

The fractional coordinates are referred to this input frame, and the relation to the standard frame is given by q_standard = P q_input + s. The transformation matrix P has rows (2/3, -1/3, -1/3), (1/3, 1/3, -2/3), and (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). Thus the standard rhombohedral coordinates are obtained directly from the input fractional coordinates by this linear transformation without any translation of origin. All positional values are rounded to five decimal places where applicable, and no precision corrections are required for any atom in this description.

In the standard setting, lithium occupies the 3a Wyckoff position with representative fractional coordinates (0, 0, 0) and multiplicity three, corresponding to the fixed coordinate relation (0, 0, 0). Iron occupies the independent 3b position with representative coordinates (0, 0, 1/2), also of multiplicity three and with no free positional parameters. Oxygen occupies the 6c position, with representative coordinates (0, 0, z), where the single independent parameter is z = 0.24042; this orbit has multiplicity six and therefore accounts for two oxygen atoms per primitive input cell after the rhombohedral centering and symmetry relations are applied.

Taken together, the atomic arrangement consists of a lithium sublattice fixed at the origin-type 3a sites, an iron sublattice on the distinct 3b sites displaced to z = 1/2 along the rhombohedral axis, and an oxygen sublattice on the 6c sites generated from (0, 0, 0.24042) by the R-3m symmetry operations. The three independent orbits fully determine the structure: Li at 3a, Fe at 3b, and O at 6c with z = 0.24042, all embedded in the specified primitive rhombohedral input lattice and related to the standard frame by the stated transformation.
